study_identification_part.si4_title: Using normative modeling to assess pharmacological treatment effect on brain state in patients with schizophrenia

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Build sex-specific normative models from Cam-CAN to quantify individual deviations in static (aFCS) and dynamic (fFCS) functional connectivity, test associations with symptoms, and assess how antipsychotic treatment changes deviation distributions in schizophrenia.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper clearly states that the normative model was built using the Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience (Cam-CAN) dataset, a large population-based study of healthy adult lifespan.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Data used in the preparation of this work were obtained from the Cam-CAN repository (available at http://www.mrc-cbu.cam. ac.uk/datasets/camcan/) (Shafto et al. 2014; Taylor et al. 2017) ( n =652). The Cam-CAN is a large population-based study of the healthy adult life span.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Two patient subgroups emerged: a normalized group with milder baseline symptoms and a deviation group; baseline depressive and overall symptoms predicted greater normalization of aFCS deviations, while baseline positive and overall symptoms predicted normalization of fFCS deviations; treatment reduced deviations in average FC more than in dynamic fluctuations.
